{
  "root_cause": "The header component incorrectly sets aria-hidden=true on the navigation menu when the menu button is not visible (desktop view), removing the navigation links from the accessibility tree.",
  "repair_strategy": "Update the init method to compute the initial visibility of the menu based on whether the menu button is hidden (indicating desktop) or the presence of the 'govuk-header__navigation--open' class, ensuring aria-hidden reflects actual visibility.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "src/govuk/components/header/header.js",
      "sha256": "33e331b7a1f44087522e90d1e295dbc0f915c8b8a82e8afd57a794d21fff4424",
      "before": "\n  this.syncState(this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open'))\n  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))",
      "after": "\n  const isVisible = !this.$menuButton.offsetParent || this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')\n  this.syncState(isVisible)\n  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))"
    }
  ],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Navigation links will be exposed as links with correct name and role, allowing keyboard and screen‑reader users to reach them via Tab.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "If the menu button's display property is changed for reasons other than viewport width, visibility detection may be incorrect.",
    "Future changes to the CSS that affect the button's layout could break the offsetParent check.",
    "The component continues to rely on the open class for mobile menu state; ensuring that class toggling remains correct is essential."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "On desktop width, verify that the navigation menu has aria-hidden=false and the menu button has aria-expanded=false.",
    "On mobile width, verify that clicking the menu button toggles the open class, aria-expanded, and aria-hidden appropriately.",
    "Confirm that Tab navigation reaches the #nav-apply element with role='link' and name='Apply' in both viewport states.",
    "Ensure that the menu button remains functional for showing/hiding the menu on mobile."
  ]
}

In observed after: nameHint:"Apply", role:null. Indeed after field shows role:null. So the accessibility tree didn't expose role as link for that element. Why? Thus navigation is not hidden. Then why role null? Possibly because the header script adds some behavior that hides the navigation when menu button is not expanded? In mobile view, the navigation is hidden via CSS display:none unless .govuk-header__navigation--open class added. But at desktop width (>40.0525em), the navigation is displayed as inline-block (since .govuk-header__navigation-item display:inline-block). The menu button is display:none. However the JS may still be adding aria-hidden? Let's check header.js: It toggles class 'govuk-header__navigation--open' on the menu when button clicked, and sets aria-expanded on button and aria-hidden on menu based on visibility. Initially, the menu does NOT have the open class (since it's hidden? Actually at desktop, the navigation is visible by default, but the script may assume it's hidden initially? Let's see init: syncState(this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open')). If the menu does not have that class, isVisible = false, then syncState sets aria-expanded=false on button, and aria-hidden=true on menu. That would hide the menu from assistive tech even though visually it's visible (due to CSS). That explains role null: because aria-hidden=true on the ul removes its descendants from accessibility tree. Thus the bug: On desktop, the navigation should be visible and not hidden; the script incorrectly assumes it's hidden unless the open class is present. The CSS for desktop shows navigation items as inline-block regardless of open class. The open class likely only affects mobile display (block vs none). So we need to adjust the script to not set aria-hidden based on open class when viewport is wide enough, or better: determine initial visibility based on whether the menu is actually visible (offsetHeight > 0) or not hidden via CSS. Simpler: Remove the aria-hidden attribute altogether? According to WAI-ARIA, menubar should have aria-hidden=false when visible. The navigation is essentially a menubar. We could just not manage aria-hidden; let it be default (false). Or we could conditionally set aria-hidden only when the menu is not visible (i.e., when the menu button is displayed). Since menu button is display:none on desktop, we can detect if $menuButton.offsetParent === null (i.e., not displayed). If button is hidden, we assume menu is visible and should not be hidden.
